bc_lifestyles.blurb: Lifestyles is a small basalt crag among the Comox Lake cliffs on Vancouver Island. It holds five routes, four of them bolted and one trad line. The grades start around 5.5 and run through the 5.7 to 5.10 range, with a single hard sport route at 5.12, so there is something for newer leaders as well as strong ones. The wall sits well above the lake, and sunlight reaches it only in patches filtered by the trees. The walk in is short and uses a climbers' trail from the main parking area. It suits a quick half day, or an add-on to the busier faces nearby.

bc_cataracta_wall.blurb: Cataracta Wall is a newer basalt wall in the Comox Lake climbing area on Vancouver Island, a short way east of the Raven's Wall trail. All five routes are bolted sport lines, graded from 5.9 up to 5.11, with the bulk of them at 5.10 and 5.11. A few of the lines run to more than one pitch, which is uncommon for this lake's mostly single-pitch cliffs, so bring a rope that suits the longer ones. The base is close to a small waterfall and a wooden staircase.

bc_ramparts_creek_main.blurb: Ramparts Creek Main is the principal wall at the Ramparts Creek crags, a sub-alpine spot at roughly 1,060 m on Vancouver Island, reached from the Strathcona Parkway road toward Mount Washington. It has five routes: three trad lines at about 5.6, 5.7 and 5.8, and two bolted sport lines around 5.10. That makes it a reasonable choice for climbers who want moderate gear leads with a couple of harder face options alongside. The place sees few visitors; bring a standard trad rack.

bc_maple_crag.blurb: Maple Crag is a small trad cliff on Constitution Hill, Vancouver Island, at about 330 m elevation. It is the first wall you meet at the spur road, with a boulder-strewn slope below and a square, blocky roof that stands out from a distance. Five routes are trad only, split between 5.9 and 5.10: two at 5.9 and three at 5.10, running from 5.10- to 5.10c. Two of the lines are regarded as the best on the wall. Since it is quick to reach, it works as a short outing or a warm-up before heading to the taller cliffs above.

bc_middle_totem.blurb: Middle Totem is a steep wall on Constitution Hill, Vancouver Island, at about 440 m, set above a viewpoint on the climbers' trail. The face is split by several clean crack lines and holds five routes: four trad and one bolted sport line. Grades cluster at 5.10, with one easier line near 5.7 and a single 5.11 sport route. Two of the trad climbs here are among the most sought-after on the hill. Expect sustained crack climbing that calls for a full rack and a confident lead head.

bc_laughlan_buttress.blurb: Laughlan Buttress is a trad buttress at the foot of the talus on Constitution Hill, Vancouver Island, visible from the parking area off to the right of the Totem cliffs. It has five trad routes, all in the harder range: two at 5.10, two at 5.11 and one at 5.12. Its best-known line stretches to five pitches and is considered one of the finest outings on the hill, so a rack and a rope for longer days are worth bringing. The main trail toward the Totems leads to the base, and this is the first cliff on that path.
